newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth group nabs northeast Brazil cellular deal.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth group nabs northeast Brazil cellular deal.

text.p: A group led by Baby Bell BellSouth Corp. has won a contract to operate cellular services in six northeastern Brazilian states with a bid of $512 million, a Brazilian government official said Friday.
The deal will enable BellSouth to enter a market of 25 million potential customers that until now has had limited access to traditional telephone service.
The 15-year contract spans Brazil's rural northeastern states of Alagoas, Ceara, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Piaui and Rio Grande do Norte.

BellSouth has moved aggressively in recent years to enter the burgeoning market for wireless phone services, which are often used by Latin Americans as their primary phone connection, due to a shortage of conventional telephone line infrastructure in the region.
The BellSouth-led BCE group also includes Brazil's Banco Safra, media group Estado de Sao Paulo and phone equipment maker Splice, all of Brazil.

Last month, the same partners won the lucrative contract to provide wireless services in Sao Paulo, the world's third-largest city, with a hefty $2.45 billion bid whose size stunned the telecommunications industry.
The BSE group said it plans to invest $450 million over the next three years to build and operate its network. The system is expected to begin offering service next year.

BellSouth already delivers wireless phone services in Argentina, Venezula, Chile and Uruguary, and is aggressively building networks to offer services in Peru, Panama, Nicauragua and Brazil, either through partnerships or wholly owned units.
BellSouth's total wireless phone concessions cover about 124 million potential customers in Central and South America, including the 25 million people living in northeast Brazil.

The company's revenues from its Latin American operations climbed to $186 million in the second quarter ended in June, up 76.7 percent from a year earlier, while the number of customers served in the region doubled to 743,000.
"Today's announcement further cements BellSouth's position as the pre-eminent wireless company in Latin America," said Charles Miller, president of BellSouth International.
BellSouth fell 25 cents to $46.19 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, dragged down with other phone industry stocks amid a steep decline in the broader market.
